# mio CLI — machine-readable command index
# Format: mio <resource> [sub-resource] <action> — purpose
# Auth: export MIO_API_KEY=mio_sk_live_<key>  (exit 3 if missing/invalid)
#       resolution order: --api-key flag > MIO_API_KEY env > OS-keychain key (mio login); --anonymous forces unauthenticated — it SENDS the request with no Authorization header and lets the API answer (a 401 under it is the server's verdict, not a local precondition; whoami reports key_source "none (--anonymous)"), an explicit --api-key still wins (MIO-2694)
#       key auth works against https://api.member.dev; override with MIO_API_BASE_URL or --api-base
# Config: TOML at ~/.config/mio/config.toml ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mio/config.toml); keys: current_team|current_hub|api_base
# Output: JSON by default when piped; --output json|table|plain; --jq <expr>; --raw for envelope
# Destructive ops (delete|cancel|refund|member-moderation: ban|unban|warn|soft-ban|community moderation reports resolve): require --yes/-y in non-interactive shells (exit 5 otherwise). restore is an undo, not destructive — no --yes needed.
# Exit codes: 0=ok 1=error 2=bad-args(400/409/422) 3=auth(401/403) 4=not-found 5=needs-confirm 6=rate-limited(429) 7=server(5xx)
# Full reference: mio gen-docs --dir ./docs  (one Markdown file per command)
# Agent skill: mio skills print (the full hub-authoring recipe + render-contract traps); mio skills install drops it into Claude Code/Codex
#
# PAGE-TREE RENDER CONTRACT (the API validates STRUCTURE, not RENDERABILITY — these all 200 and render nothing):
#   node envelope: {id, kind, template?, value?, settings{}, children[]} — VALUE IS TOP-LEVEL, NOT settings.value (the #1 silent drop; progress-ring is the sole kind reading settings.value)
#   the renderer dispatches on `kind`, never `type`; `template` marks a section (publish-time conversion + surface wrapping); no defaults cascade — inline every value; exactly one level:1 headline per page (extras demote to h2)
#   leaf kinds (complete): headline text image video button icon divider progress-ring. NOT node kinds: subheadline paragraph embed html spacer stat input sidebar section (removed from the FE or never existed — authoring one renders blank; use headline level:3, text, and container gap instead). content-grid is a TEMPLATE id, not a kind. A sidebar = a `row` whose `stack` children set settings.width (full|1/2|1/3|2/3|1/4|3/4)
#   settings.weight must be a NUMBER (700), never "bold"; section `template` must be a non-empty string — `pages tree set` rejects both client-side (exit 2, no HTTP)
#   button: value=label; settings.action={"type":"url|page|email|scroll|playlist","value":"<canonical, no scheme prefix, no #>"}; icon: value=glyph name (NOT settings.name); image/video: value=the URL
#   settings.surface = {padding, background, gradient}. background.type enum: tint (light tint of branding.secondary — the only value scaffolds emit) | color+token(primary|secondary|accent|muted|background; primary also stamps data-bg="primary" → bold band + primary-button auto-inversion) | custom-color+value(#rrggbb) | gradient | image+url(+blur) | none | thumbnail(accepted, no-op). TRAP: an INVALID background.type is accepted on publish and renders a TRANSPARENT row with NO error (renderer default case) (MIO-2663)
#   TRAP: the gradient config is a SIBLING of background — surface.gradient, NOT surface.background.gradient; nesting it silently falls back to the default `split`. gradient.type: monochrome|analogous|complementary|triadic|split|warm-shift|custom (custom REQUIRES customStart+customEnd 6-digit hex, else falls back to split)
#   `mio pages publish` returns section_count — compare it to the number of sections you authored; that, not the 200, is the "did it apply" signal (MIO-2539)
#
# HUB BRANDING KEY MAP: primary=buttons/links/CTAs; secondary=SECTION HEADINGS (h1-h3) AND the base of every surface.background:{"type":"tint"} block (set it light and every heading goes invisible — the most common branding mistake); text=body copy; background=page background; header_color/header_accent=top-nav bg+accent (emitted raw, no contrast correction); dark_mode=bool. Colors must be 6-DIGIT hex (3- and 8-digit are rejected by the FE parser, which then silently uses its own defaults). Theme: branding.dark_mode+background is the reliable CLI lever; the FE also honors settings.theme.mode (light|dark|custom) and it WINS over branding.dark_mode, but `theme` is not on the settings-key allowlist so it warns (and still sends) — don't pair it with --strict-keys
# NAV ICON GLYPHS (MIO-2675, CLI passes them through unvalidated): header/footer accept any id from the hub FE icon sprite (~205; generated ICON_NAMES in mio-hub src/components/ui/icon.tsx is authoritative) and `icon` is OPTIONAL — an unknown name drops the icon, not the item; `info` and `globe` DO NOT EXIST (use information/information-circle, earth/global). mobile accepts an 8-VALUE WHITELIST and `icon` is MANDATORY (off-list → the whole tab is dropped): Home Bell User Users MessageSquare MessageCircle Search content — FE component names, not sprite ids, casing significant. <3 valid mobile tabs → the FE replaces the list with its defaults; >5 → truncated to 5

mio version — print version information
mio update — self-update mio; --version pins a release; --prefix chooses install dir; also refreshes an unmodified installed agent skill. macOS/Linux rerun the official release installer; Windows updates natively (download + SHA-256 verify against checksums.txt + binary swap) with no sh/curl dependency, leaving mio.exe.old behind until the next run
mio skills install — install the embedded mio agent skill into your coding agent; --target claude|codex (default claude); --user (default) or --project; --force overwrites a hand-edited file; idempotent
mio skills print — print the embedded mio agent skill (SKILL.md) to stdout; --target claude|codex
mio login — interactive login (stores key; auto-resolves team for single-team accounts); use MIO_API_KEY instead in agents
mio register — create a new account (email+password, optional --first-name/--last-name; or MIO_EMAIL/MIO_PASSWORD) then auto-login (mints+stores a key, REPLACING any stored key); unauthenticated; in agents prefer a pre-provisioned MIO_API_KEY
mio whoami — print resolved user, active team, hub, api-base, profile, and key source; use as "did my setup work?" check
mio logout — clear stored credentials

mio config set — set a config value (keys: current_team, current_hub, api_base; validated as UUID / http(s) URL)
mio config get — get a config value
mio config list — list all config values

mio api-keys create — create a new API key for the current team (secret returned once)
mio api-keys list — list API keys for the current team
mio api-keys retrieve — retrieve a single API key by id
mio api-keys delete — revoke an API key by id

mio teams create — create a new team
mio teams list — list teams the authenticated user belongs to
mio teams retrieve — retrieve a team by id
mio teams update — update team attributes
mio teams delete — delete a team
mio teams switch — server-side team switch AND updates local CLI context (writes team to config, clears hub)
mio teams members list — list members of a team
mio teams members add — add a user to a team
mio teams members remove — remove a user from a team

mio users me — retrieve the authenticated user's own profile
mio users list — list users
mio users retrieve — retrieve a user by id
mio users update — update a user's attributes

mio roles create — create a custom role
mio roles list — list roles
mio roles retrieve — retrieve a role by id
mio roles update — update a role
mio roles delete — delete a role
mio roles permissions list — list all available permissions
mio roles permissions assign — assign a permission to a role by --slug (flat {slug} body; requires user-JWT auth, API keys are rejected 401)
mio roles permissions remove — remove a permission from a role (positional role_id + permission_slug; destructive, needs --yes; user-JWT only)

mio hubs * — the hub id is an OPTIONAL positional on every hubs verb except `delete`: precedence positional > --hub > current_hub in config > single-hub auto-default, so `mio hubs retrieve <id>`, `mio hubs retrieve --hub <id>` and a bare `mio hubs retrieve` are all valid. Covers retrieve/update/policies update/policies gate/redirect-origins get|set/email-settings get|update/navigation list|add|remove|reorder. When no hub resolves from any source the error names all three sources (never Cobra's "accepts 1 arg(s), received 0"). EXCEPTION: `hubs delete` still requires the id positionally — irreversible, so it never takes its target from ambient context (MIO-2732)
mio hubs create — create a new hub within the active team; author the presentation layer via --branding-json/--navigation-json/--settings-json/--meta-json (opaque JSONB objects; inline JSON or @file); --logo-url and --favicon-url merge into branding rather than replacing it. Unknown keys in --branding-json/--settings-json/--meta-json WARN by default (stderr) and ERROR under --strict-keys (best-effort allowlist — the API stores these blobs verbatim with no schema, and the hub frontend is the authoritative render contract; accepted keys are in each flag's --help and docs/internal/api-surface.md) (MIO-2515). EXCEPTION to "verbatim": branding.logo_url and branding.favicon_url ARE validated server-side — an absolute https:// URL is required and data:/javascript: URLs are rejected (MIO-2658), so a data: SVG logo fails while every other branding key round-trips unchecked. Output includes a derived published (=!is_private); in table mode a private hub also prints a stderr hint with the slug and how to publish (--published). No public URL is echoed — the API returns no domain/url field and the CLI knows only the API base, so a URL is not derivable client-side (MIO-2521, MIO-2522)
mio hubs list — list hubs in the active team
mio hubs retrieve — retrieve a hub by id; output includes derived convenience booleans registration_enabled (=settings.registration.enabled===true, fail-closed) and published (=!is_private), mirroring the backend's derived policies_enabled; --raw bypasses them (MIO-2516, MIO-2521)
mio hubs update — update hub attributes; --navigation-json authors the header/footer menu (whole-blob replace, typed items validated); --branding-json/--settings-json/--meta-json deep-merge (read-modify-write, sibling keys preserved); --logo-url and --favicon-url merge into branding (all inline JSON or @file). --registration-enabled true|false sets settings.registration.enabled via RMW (gated on Changed() so =false ≠ unset; sibling keys preserved) (MIO-2516). --unset <dotted.path> DELETES a blob key (the only real delete — *-json flags are merge-only: null persists as null, {} is a no-op); first segment selects the blob (branding/settings/meta), nested paths supported, repeatable + comma-separated; blank/bare-blob/unknown-blob paths are usage errors that fire no request (MIO-2517). Apply order per blob: (1) *-json merge, (2) scalar flags, (3) --unset LAST (unset wins over a same-command merge). Unknown keys in the merged blobs WARN by default and ERROR under --strict-keys (only the keys you supply are checked, never the hub's existing stored blob; MIO-2515)
mio hubs delete — delete a hub; the hub id MUST be positional (no --hub/current_hub fallback — irreversible)
mio hubs navigation list/add/remove/reorder — edit the hub menu item-by-item without rebuilding the whole --navigation-json blob (RMW the navigation blob: GET hub, mutate one bucket, PATCH navigation as a whole-blob replace). Buckets: header/footer/mobile. Items have no stable id → addressed by zero-based INDEX (from 'list'). add [hub_id] <bucket> takes --item-json '<obj>' (any bucket/type; inline or @file) OR the url convenience --type url --href <h> --label <l> (header/footer only — mobile items {id,label,route,icon} must use --item-json), plus --position to insert (default append); remove [hub_id] <bucket> --index N; reorder [hub_id] <bucket> --order 2,0,1 (a permutation, every index once). The hub id shares the positional slot with the bucket: a lone header|footer|mobile is read as the BUCKET and the hub comes from --hub/current_hub (`mio hubs navigation add header --type url …`), so `list` accepts 0-2 positionals and add/remove/reorder 1-2 (MIO-2732). Item `icon` values are NOT validated by the CLI and use two different vocabularies — see the NAV ICON GLYPHS header note above (header/footer = the FE sprite ids, optional; mobile = an 8-name whitelist, mandatory). Re-validates the whole menu (typed header/footer items, hub-scoped hrefs) before writing; usage errors fire no PATCH. No optimistic-lock guard — last-write-wins, same as --navigation-json (MIO-2633)
mio hubs scaffold — build a full-experience hub in ONE idempotent command from a template: --template community applies branding+favicon, a typed navigation menu (hub-relative hrefs auto-scoped to /{slug}), settings.registration.enabled, discussion spaces, an onboarding contact-attribute schema, playlists (published visible), and a homepage (page-builder catalog template → page create + tree set). Create mode: --name/--slug (a new private hub). Resume/target mode: --hub <id> (also resumes a partially-built hub — steps are idempotent: spaces/onboarding skip-if-exists, playlists skip if the hub already has published ones). --dry-run prints the ordered plan with no changes. --publish (default OFF; the hub stays private for review) sets is_private:false at the end. --favicon-url/--logo-url/--registration-enabled override the template. PALETTE (MIO-2604): --primary-color/--secondary-color/--text-color/--background-color/--header-color/--header-accent/--social-image-url, plus --branding-json for a whole object, MERGE over the template's branding block (a key you do not name keeps the template's value); precedence is template → --branding-json → scalar flags, matching how --logo-url/--favicon-url already beat --branding-json on hubs update. CASCADE: --primary-color also fills header_color unless YOU gave a header color (--header-color, or a header_color key in --branding-json) — the template's own header_color does not suppress it, because the community template sets header_color to its primary and yielding to it would leave a rebranded hub with the template's header. Color VALUES are passed through unvalidated (branding is opaque JSONB with no server-side format contract, and the frontend accepts named colors/rgb()/gradients), while the KEYS are strict-checked pre-auth against the MIO-2515 allowlist so a typo exits 2 with no request. --dry-run names the palette it would apply; the json result carries branding_overrides (the resolved layer, cascade included; {} when none). Backend-gated steps (welcome post MIO-2262, auto-assign-admin MIO-2540) are skipped-with-note until those endpoints land. Delegates to the existing CLI verbs' internals (CLI-only, no raw REST), so template values pass the same validation as the individual commands — a malformed key errors instead of silently dropping. Output honors -o json|table|plain like every other command (MIO-2574): json/plain (json is the default off a TTY) emit a machine-readable result — hub_id, hub_slug, hub_name, hub_path, published, template_id, catalog_revision, homepage_page_id, and pages/spaces/onboarding_attributes/playlists/policies carrying the ids this run created or recovered — so `mio hubs scaffold … --jq .hub_id` captures the new hub id directly; table renders the human summary. Every progress note, catalog provenance line and recovery hint goes to stderr, so a json stdout is always parseable; if a step fails after the hub was created, the error itself names the hub id (nothing is rolled back). The public URL is host-relative — the API returns no domain/url (MIO-2543)
mio hubs templates — list the built-in hub scaffold templates (e.g. community); honors -o json|table and --jq
mio hubs policies update — create or replace a hub legal policy (tos or privacy_policy); hub id is an OPTIONAL positional (falls back to --hub/current_hub); --content supports @file; --require-acceptance for tos only
mio hubs policies gate — toggle hub policy enforcement (settings.policies.enabled); optional positional hub id (falls back to --hub/current_hub); --enabled required and explicit (--enabled or --enabled=false). There is no admin policies READ (the only /policies GET is the member portal route, which rejects API keys), so no `policies get`
mio hubs redirect-origins get — read the magic-link redirect-origin allowlist for a hub (owner-only; optional positional hub id, falls back to --hub/current_hub)
mio hubs redirect-origins set — full-replace the redirect-origin allowlist; optional positional hub id (falls back to --hub/current_hub); provide --origins (comma-separated) or --clear to empty it

mio automations create — create a draft automation in a hub; --name --re-entry-mode never|after_exit|interval --definition (JSON or @file: {triggers,nodes,edges}) --settings
mio automations list — list automations in a hub; --filter-status (draft|active|paused) --page-size --page-after
mio automations retrieve — retrieve an automation by id
mio automations update — update a draft automation's name/definition/settings
mio automations publish — validate + snapshot the draft as an immutable version (publish before activate)
mio automations activate — activate a published automation (draft/paused → active)
mio automations deactivate — deactivate an automation (active → paused)
mio automations versions — list published versions of an automation
mio automations enrollments — list enrollment runs; --filter-status (active|stuck|completed)
mio automations enroll — manually enroll a contact; --team-contact-id
mio automations fire-event — fire a custom trigger event; --event-type --team-contact-id --idempotency-key (all required) --payload
mio automations test — dry-run a contact through the published graph, no side effects; --team-contact-id

mio webhook-endpoints create — register an outbound webhook endpoint (SSRF-guarded); --name --target-url --signing-secret (optional, write-only)
mio webhook-endpoints list — list webhook endpoints in a hub
mio webhook-endpoints delete — delete a webhook endpoint by id; --yes in non-interactive shells

mio content create — create a content node in a hub
mio content list — list root-level content nodes in a hub

mio content children — list child nodes of a content node

mio content restore — restore a soft-deleted content node

mio pages create — create a page in a hub; flags: --title --slug --type --privacy (public|members|private) --position --is-home (sends is_homepage) --settings/--meta (@file). NO --published/--description/--layout (not in schema). --privacy DEFAULTS TO members: omit it and the page is login-walled, which is how a hub ships looking public and isn't (hubs scaffold sets it, MIO-2563; this manual path does not). `home` is a RESERVED slug (rejected) and an omitted --slug fails "Field required" — use a real slug (welcome/start/about) and designate the homepage with --is-home
mio pages list — list pages in a hub
mio pages retrieve — retrieve a page by id; add --tree to get the raw published node tree (page-trees resource, resolve=false) for admin editor use
mio pages update — update a page
mio pages delete — delete a page
mio pages home — retrieve the hub's home page
mio pages publish — publish a page draft; requires --if-match <draft_version> (read draft_version from a prior retrieve for optimistic concurrency)
mio pages sections create — add a section to a page; --type is validated against the catalog writable section types (see 'pages catalog section-types --writable-only')
mio pages sections list — list sections on a page
mio pages sections update — update a section
mio pages sections delete — delete a section from a page
mio pages sections reorder — reorder sections on a page
mio pages tree get — get a page's author draft node-tree (audience=author, resolve=true); draft_version is the OCC token for 'tree set'/'publish'. RESPONSE SHAPE ≠ WRITE SHAPE: get answers {"id":...,"tree":{"root":...},"draft_version":N} while set --file wants the tree object itself, {"root":...} — unwrap with --jq .tree; feeding a get response straight back is rejected
mio pages tree set — replace a page's draft node-tree from --file (a tree JSON, {"root":{...}}); --if-match <draft_version> is OPTIONAL and defaults to 0 — omit it for the FIRST tree on a draft-less page (whose 'tree get' 404s, so there is no version to read back); pass the current draft_version for later sets (a defaulted 0 against a page that already has a draft is a 409 conflict, never a clobber). A page created by `hubs scaffold` ALREADY HAS A DRAFT (draft_version 1, not 0), so your first write against one needs --if-match 1 — never guess, read it back with `mio pages tree get <id> --jq .draft_version`. Every node needs an "id": scaffold mints fresh UUIDv7s, so splice scaffolded subtrees rather than hand-writing nodes (there is no id-minting helper); "root"/"hero" style outline markers are not valid ids
mio pages catalog * — the group has exactly THREE verbs: scaffold, templates, section-types. THERE IS NO `pages catalog list`
mio pages catalog scaffold — scaffold a node-tree from a catalog template (Go applier); --template <id> [--variant <v>]; page templates emit {"root":...} for 'tree set', section templates emit a bare node; emit-only (offline-capable; --offline forces vendored, --catalog <file> overrides). PAGE templates are OUTLINES: page-homepage's hero child arrives as {"kind":"row","template":"hero","settings":{}} with no surface and no values — scaffold the page for the skeleton, then scaffold each SECTION separately for the real DS-conformed recipe and splice it into root.children. `row` is the unified 1-4 column section; --variant picks the layout: 1col|2eq|2left|2right|3eq|4eq|bound-cards|cta-band|faq (hero/grid/compact carry variants too — `pages catalog templates` prints them)
mio pages catalog templates — list catalog author templates + their variants; --page-type <pt> shows the section templates recommended for that page type (ordered) + its page template
mio pages catalog section-types — list catalog compiled section types; --writable-only lists just the imperative-door allow-list

mio media files list — list team media files (cursor-paginated); --limit --after
mio media files retrieve — retrieve a media file by id (POSITIONAL)
mio media files durable-url — print a file's durable (non-expiring) hub-scoped image URL(s) to inline into a page-tree image node; joins durable_variants[preset] with the REQUIRED ?hub_id=; --hub required, --preset (omit=all presets), --publish also publishes the file public to the hub so the URL resolves; image-only (MIO-2514, backend MIO-2525/#533)
mio media files update — update file metadata; --title --description --visibility --folder-id
mio media files delete — soft-delete a file; --yes
mio media files upload — upload a file end-to-end from the CLI (create → presigned S3 PUT → finalize; auto-multipart for large files); path is POSITIONAL; --title --mime-type --folder-id --wait --timeout --multipart --part-size-mb
mio media files replace — replace an existing file's underlying asset; <file_id> <path> POSITIONAL; single-part finalizes at .../replace/{replacement_id}/finalize, but multipart replace ENDS at the terminal .../replace/{replacement_id}/multipart/{upload_id}/complete (no separate finalize); --mime-type --filename --multipart --part-size-mb
mio media files finalize — finalize a file after its presigned upload (POST .../finalize); file id POSITIONAL
mio media files transcode — (re)start transcoding for a file (POST .../transcode); file id POSITIONAL
mio media files register-synthetic — register a synthetic (document/pdf) file; --title (required) --asset-kind (document|pdf) --visibility --mime-type --original-filename --description
mio media files cards get — list a file's in-video CTA cards; file id POSITIONAL
mio media files cards set — replace a file's CTA cards (full-list PUT); --cards (JSON array or @file)
mio media files chapters get — list a file's effective chapters (authored else auto); file id POSITIONAL
mio media files chapters set — replace a file's authored chapters (full-list PUT); --chapters (JSON array or @file)
mio media folders list — list team media folders (cursor-paginated); --limit --after
mio media folders create — create a folder; --name (required) --parent-id
mio media folders retrieve — retrieve a folder by id (POSITIONAL)
mio media folders update — rename a folder; --name
mio media folders delete — soft-delete an empty folder; --yes
mio media folders move — move a folder subtree to a new parent or root; folder id POSITIONAL; exactly one of --parent-id / --to-root
mio media search — hybrid (lexical+semantic) search over the team's media transcripts; --query (required) --hub-id --limit (1-100)
mio media playlists list — list team media playlists (cursor-paginated); --limit --after
mio media playlists create — create a playlist; --title (required) --description --visibility --hub-id
mio media playlists retrieve — retrieve a playlist by id (POSITIONAL)
mio media playlists update — update a playlist; --title --description --visibility --hub-id --podcast-feed-enabled
mio media playlists delete — soft-delete a playlist; --yes
mio media playlists set-cover — set (replace) a playlist's cover from a media file; playlist id POSITIONAL; --file-id (required; the FILE id — its media_id is resolved automatically) --position
mio media playlists items add — add a media file to a playlist; --playlist-id --file-id --position (0-based; omit → position 0/front; negative rejected client-side)
mio media playlists items list — list a playlist's items in order (cursor-paginated); --playlist-id
mio media playlists items remove — remove an item by its item id (the 'id' from 'items list', not the file id); --playlist-id --yes
mio media playlists items reorder — move an item to a new position; item id is POSITIONAL; --playlist-id --position (required, >= 0)
mio media hub-media publish — publish a standalone file to the active hub (writes a hub_media row); --file-id (required) --visibility --published-at --position
mio media hub-media list — list files published to the active hub; cursor-paginated
mio media hub-media unpublish — remove a file's hub_media row from the active hub; file id POSITIONAL; --yes
mio media hub-playlists publish — publish a playlist to the active hub (writes a hub_media row); --playlist-id (required) --visibility --published-at --position
mio media hub-playlists list — list playlists published to the active hub; cursor-paginated
mio media hub-playlists unpublish — remove a playlist's hub_media row from the active hub; playlist id POSITIONAL; --yes
mio media attachments list — list media attachment rows; --media-id --target-type --target-id (cursor-paginated)
mio media attachments show — retrieve an attachment by id (POSITIONAL)
mio media attachments update — update an attachment's --role and/or --position; attachment id POSITIONAL
mio media attachments delete — delete an attachment row; attachment id POSITIONAL; --yes
mio media transcripts get — get a media's transcript (media_id POSITIONAL)
mio media transcripts vtt — get the transcript as WebVTT (media_id POSITIONAL)
mio media transcripts content — get the transcript plain-text content (media_id POSITIONAL)
mio media transcripts versions — list transcript versions, or retrieve one; media_id POSITIONAL, optional [version]
mio media transcripts edit — replace a transcript's words (creates a new version); media_id POSITIONAL; --words (JSON array or @file) --language
mio media transcripts revert — revert a transcript to a prior version; media_id POSITIONAL; --version (required, >= 1)

mio products create — create a product
mio products list — list products in the active team
mio products retrieve — retrieve a product by id
mio products update — update a product
mio products delete — delete a product
mio products prices create — create a price for a product; product id is a POSITIONAL arg: mio products prices create <product_id> --amount 4900 --currency usd --interval month [--nickname ...]
mio products prices list — list prices for a product; product id is a POSITIONAL arg: mio products prices list <product_id>
mio products prices retrieve — retrieve a price by id
mio products prices update — update a price
mio products prices delete — delete a price

mio checkout orders list — list orders in a hub
mio checkout orders retrieve — retrieve an order by id
mio checkout subscriptions list — list subscriptions in a hub
mio checkout subscriptions retrieve — retrieve a subscription by id
mio checkout subscriptions cancel — cancel a subscription
mio checkout payments list — list payments in a hub
mio checkout payments retrieve — retrieve a payment by id
mio checkout payments refund — issue a refund for a payment
mio checkout webhooks list — list payment webhook events
mio checkout webhooks retrieve — retrieve a webhook event by id
mio checkout webhooks replay — replay a payment webhook event
mio checkout accounts list — list connected payment accounts
mio checkout accounts retrieve — retrieve a payment account by id
mio checkout accounts onboarding-link — WEB/JWT-ONLY, always fails from this CLI (exit 3): the backend rejects API-key principals on this route (leaked key must not attach a payout account) and this CLI is API-key-only; connect Stripe via the member.dev dashboard instead
mio checkout stripe-sync import — start a Stripe data import for the active team
mio checkout stripe-sync import-status — check the status of a Stripe import run
mio checkout stripe-sync adopt-product — adopt an existing Stripe product into mio

mio email drip-campaigns create — create a drip campaign; enrollment flags: --enrollment-mode event|segment|both, --trigger-event-type, --segment-id, --segment-check-interval-minutes, --allow-reenrollment
mio email drip-campaigns list — list drip campaigns
mio email drip-campaigns retrieve — retrieve a drip campaign by id
mio email drip-campaigns update — update a drip campaign; same enrollment flags as create
mio email drip-campaigns delete — delete a drip campaign
mio email drip-campaigns activate — activate a paused or draft drip campaign
mio email drip-campaigns pause — pause an active drip campaign
mio email steps create — add a step to a drip campaign
mio email steps list — list steps in a drip campaign
mio email steps update — update a drip campaign step
mio email steps delete — delete a step from a drip campaign
mio email templates create — create an email template
mio email templates list — list email templates
mio email templates retrieve — retrieve a template by id
mio email templates update — update an email template
mio email templates delete — delete an email template
mio email templates preview — render a preview of an email template
mio email config set — configure outbound email (SMTP / provider settings)
mio email config get — retrieve current email configuration
mio email config delete — remove email configuration
mio email config test — send a test email to verify configuration
mio email enrollments list — list contacts enrolled in a drip campaign
mio email enrollments exit — remove a contact from a drip campaign enrollment
mio email stats get — retrieve email send/open/click stats for a hub
mio email suppressions list — list active email suppressions for the active hub
mio email suppressions create — suppress (admin_block) an email address for the active hub via --email; reason is forced to admin_block server-side
mio email suppressions lift — lift (un-suppress) a hub suppression by id; destructive, needs --yes. NOTE: the hub suppression routes require platform_admin, so team-admin API keys get 403

mio access-rules rules create — create an access rule for a hub
mio access-rules rules list — list access rules
mio access-rules rules retrieve — retrieve an access rule by id
mio access-rules rules update — update an access rule
mio access-rules rules delete — delete an access rule
mio access-rules overrides create — create an access override for a specific contact
mio access-rules overrides list — list access overrides
mio access-rules overrides retrieve — retrieve an access override by id
mio access-rules overrides update — update an access override
mio access-rules overrides delete — delete an access override

mio activity contact — retrieve activity feed for a specific contact in a hub
mio activity top-engaged — retrieve the most engaged contacts in a hub
